text:
anna_cs: FYI Acme just escalated — they ran the same rerank requests against our API before and after the weekend model push and scores changed enough to flip the top-1. They say nothing in their client changed.

liam_support: Oof. Do we have the original requests + responses from them? can we repro internally?

anna_cs: Pasted the minimal repro they sent. They call the rerank endpoint with alias `rerank-latest` (no pinned version). Example payload:```json
{
  "model": "rerank",
  "inputs": [
    {"query": "best wireless earbuds under $100", "candidates": ["brand A review", "brand B review", "budget buds comparison"] }
  ]
}```
They reported old scores (Friday) vs new (Monday):
- candidate 1: 0.87 -> 0.62
- candidate 2: 0.45 -> 0.74
- candidate 3: 0.33 -> 0.29

diego_ml: Important to note: a rerank model alias was shifted to v1.3 over weekend (we rolled an 8-bit quantized variant). Could be quantization differences or postprocessing change. Did they use `top_k` or any client-side sorting?

anna_cs: Customer says they just sort by score descending client-side. No top_k.

maya_prod: Deploy bot shows alias update at 1801998000 — `rerank-latest` -> `rerank-v1.3-8bit`. Deploy summary: `canary pass -> full deploy`. perf-monitor-bot log: slight latency increase (~12ms median) but within SLO.

deploybot: [deploy] alias `rerank-latest` updated to model `rerank-v1.3-8bit` at 1801998000 by diego_ml.

liam_support: Steps we should do: 1) repro with exact payload against both variants (v1.2 and v1.3-8bit). 2) check tokenization/normalization differences. 3) confirm no server-side postprocessing changed (score scaling, softmax, logit transform).

diego_ml: I'll run quick parity check. Repro command (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDSHIFT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rerank-v1.2","inputs":[{"query":"best wireless earbuds under $100","candidates":["brand A review","brand B review","budget buds comparison"]}]}'
```
And same with `rerank-v1.3-8bit`. I also pushed a tiny eval script to run a batch of 200 customer queries to compare score deltas.

anna_cs: Customer provided a CSV with 120 sample queries — sent to #private-acme with notes. They want urgent rollback or mitigation.

liam_support: For now we can create a per-customer alias pinned to `rerank-v1.2` and tell them we pinned them to stable. Agree?

maya_prod: Can do. Creating alias `acme-rerank-stable` -> `rerank-v1.2` now (will be effective immediately and only for that org).

deploybot: alias `acme-rerank-stable` created pointing to `rerank-v1.2` at 1802000100 by maya_prod.

diego_ml: Results from my quick parity run: for the sample query above:
- rerank-v1.2 scores: [0.872, 0.450, 0.328]
- rerank-v1.3-8bit scores: [0.621, 0.739, 0.290]
So yes, ordering flipped. Distribution across 200 samples: ~9% of queries flipped top-1, mean absolute score delta 0.17.

liam_support: That's not acceptable to the customer. Is this expected from 8-bit quant? 9% flip rate seems high for rerank tasks.

diego_ml: 8-bit quant can change logits, but our pre-release eval didn't show this magnitude for our held-out set. Two hypotheses: (A) the alias mapping included a model with different normalization head (we forgot to carry over scale layer) or (B) there was a preprocessing tokenization change in the inference pipeline for v1.3.

anna_cs: The customer insists they didn't change and their downstream UX is breaking. They asked for repro steps so their engineers can verify locally. Please add a minimal reproducible curl + example response to return to them.

diego_ml: Minimal curl + sample responses below. Note: replace API_KEY.
```bash
# v1.2 (stable)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rerank-v1.2","inputs":[{"query":"best wireless earbuds under $100","candidates":["brand A review","brand B review","budget buds comparison"]}]}' | jq

# v1.3-8bit
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rerank-v1.3-8bit","inputs":[{"query":"best wireless earbuds under $100","candidates":["brand A review","brand B review","budget buds comparison"]}]}' | jq
```
Sample outputs (truncated):
- v1.2: `{"scores": [0.872, 0.450, 0.328]}`
- v1.3-8bit: `{"scores": [0.621, 0.739, 0.290]}`

maya_prod: Confirmed we did not change any server-side sorting or apply additional score transforms in the request path. The only change was the model binary behind the alias.

liam_support: Next steps / owner? We need a short-term mitigation and a medium-term fix.

diego_ml: Short-term: keep `acme-rerank-stable` pinned; run customer-specific evaluation of their CSV to quantify impact and provide receipts. Medium-term: reproduce delta on an internal eval harness, run ablation to identify whether tokenization, final layer scaling, or quantization rounding is the driver. If it's the model, we may need to produce a quantization-aware fine-tune or keep separate quantized/stable variants.

anna_cs: I told Acme we'll pin them and run a deep dive. They've asked for ETA — can we get an initial report within 24 hours?

diego_ml: I'll own the deep dive. Plan: 1) run full CSV on v1.2 vs v1.3-8bit (in progress). 2) Dump logits + tokenization alignment for 50 largest-delta cases. 3) If tokenization differences show different token counts, that points to a preprocessing mismatch; otherwise likely quantization/final layer. Expect initial results in ~12 hours.

perf-monitor-bot: [metric] rerank-v1.3-8bit median p50 latency +12ms vs v1.2, p95 +25ms at 1802002000.

liam_support: Also logging this as a severity-3 customer escalation. I'm drafting a customer-facing note: we pinned them and are investigating root cause; will update in 12h with technical findings.

anna_cs: Thanks team. Diego add the eval output in this thread when ready and tag me and @liam_support. I'll keep Acme updated. :thumbsup:

diego_ml: Will do. uploading intermediate CSV diffs to the secure share now. Posting first 10 examples with highest score delta in 30m.

maya_prod: After Diego's triage we should revisit our deployment checklist: require regression pass on customer-surface rerank evals or ability to opt-out of quantized variants per-alias. Logging a follow-up ticket in product.

anna_cs: Good call. Closing the loop here once the 12h report is in.

deploybot: [note] rollback ready if requested. Use `rollback --alias rerank-latest --to rerank-v1.2` (ops perms required).
